findings.location: architecture/linux-host-authority/README.md line 544 (the Vectors section) and scripts/linux_host_authority.py line 4855 (replay's comment on leafVectors)
findings.finding: Both say each generated leaf vector sets the leaf's first occurrence 'to another value of its type'. 88 of the 2,043 leaf vectors do not: they set a null leaf to a string, a different JSON type. These are 53 host-authority.json member leaves of text citations (for example supersedes[LR-CAPACITY-ZERO-COST].member, LV-A0016) and the 35 decisions.decisionLines[*].supersededBy leaves that are null (for example LX-D1's), each set to "MUTATED". Every one is still refused as recorded, the member leaves by 'a text citation names no member path' and the supersededBy leaves by their pin, so the vectors are sound and replay passes; only the published description is inaccurate. Under MON-LHA-CR-CAP this is not a decision-carrying member left unchecked, so it is not MAJOR.
findings.requiredChange: c8 text-only errata: in both places, say that a leaf vector sets the leaf's first occurrence to another value of its type, or to a string where the leaf is null (or equivalent words). No vector, pin or behaviour change.

findings.location: architecture/linux-host-authority/README.md lines 70-74 (the closed-lists paragraph); scripts/linux_host_authority.py _closed callers with ordered=False (hostInventory.leftOut, packages.sources, access.leaseBindings, liveLauncher.trustMounts, launcher steps)
findings.finding: Two points about the closed lists, neither a defect in enforcement. (a) The README quotes 'an id-keyed list names each entry once' as the rule for a repeated id. In-memory probes of all 37 ID_KEYED lists (a wrong entry then a correct copy, a pure duplicate, and a new id appended) are all refused by named rules, but only the 11 lists that _closed compares refuse a repeat with that text; the other 26 refuse it first by their existing ordered comparison (for example 'every span entry has its own id', 'every signing authority is listed', 'the runbook has steps 1 to 16, each with its check'). (b) Five id-keyed lists are compared as exact sets and accept any entry order: hostInventory.leftOut (6 of 6 adjacent swaps and the reversal accepted), packages.sources, access.leaseBindings, liveLauncher.trustMounts and the launcher steps (9 of 9 swaps and the reversal). For the first four the design gives a set (the leases' time order is in their pinned window and revokedAtStep). For the launcher steps, DESIGN.r7.md line 130 calls the record 'the ordered operator steps as data', but each step's runbookStep and inputDigests are pinned, the request-before-issuance dependency is carried by inputDigests, and the published list is not in runbook order (INSTALL_LIVE_LAUNCHER, step 8, is listed last), so the design fixes no list order that the set comparison loses. All 32 other id-keyed lists with two or more entries refuse every adjacent swap.
findings.requiredChange: None required. Optionally, in the c8 errata, say that a repeat is refused by that rule or by the list's own ordered comparison, and name the lists compared as sets.

findings.location: scripts/linux_host_authority.py explain (line 4788) and main (lines 4916-4934); README.md lines 51-53
findings.finding: The C2-4 fold is right: REFUSED_ERRORS is one tuple, main runs the command through explain and has no handler of its own (a new candidate test checks both), and the usage error still exits 2 before explain. One side effect: c6's main printed the class name for any ValueError subclass (it tested type(exc) is ValueError), while c7's main goes through explain, which prints a ValueError subclass's message (isinstance). So a malformed record's JSONDecodeError on the command line now prints the decoder's message instead of 'JSONDecodeError'; it is still refused with exit 1. The author's report describes this the other way round ('explain now names ... a ValueError subclass the same way main always did'). No vector or test reaches it: the eight parse negatives all use the parser's own refusals, and explain's behaviour for ValueError subclasses is c6's.

Both memoizations are pure and change no outcome. The string memo caches only strings that passed, so a failing string is re-evaluated and keeps its path in the message, and both rules depend only on the string and the module's constant patterns. Base._derive caches the lines, sha256 and parsed JSON of a cited file per Base instance, after read() has checked CITED_FILES; the four callers (check_entry twice, the readings loop, the readiness read) only index and slice the cached values, and check_entry still calls read() first, so the cited-file refusal keeps its place. The string sets are module-global, so a future test that monkeypatched FORBIDDEN_TEXT or NAMED_TEXT would find earlier strings already marked passed; no current test patches either (the candidate test only compares FORBIDDEN_TEXT with LAB-RUNPLAN-001's).
findings.requiredChange: None. Optionally key the string memo on the pattern tuple, or note in the comment that the patterns must not be patched.

findings.finding: The generated blocks are sound and self-checking in the tree: check_pins compares every pin with _same (type for type, [*] mapped over every entry), the two new candidate tests re-enumerate the records and require every leaf in exactly one of the three blocks and every P leaf to have its vector, and replay refuses each leaf vector as recorded. The cost is in maintenance and size: the builder that generates them is outside the tree (as the PINNED block's has been since c1), every record value now also lives in the checker, so any later change to a record leaf is a regeneration of the pins and the leaf vectors, and vectors.json grew from 123,652 to 922,938 bytes and the checker from 119,039 to 353,194 bytes. That is not a CI problem here (candidate tests about 13 s on this host, the oracle under 1 s, check and replay each well inside the 120 s cap) and the generated rows are mechanical to review.
findings.requiredChange: None. Keep the c8 errata text-only or checker-only, as MON-LHA-CR-CAP says, and keep the builder with the lane's records for any later regeneration.
